title: Red-Team Tooling — Garak, Llama Guard, PyRIT

questions.question: What does guard_classify return for a matching hazard phrase in the toy?
options: A single natural-language refusal with no category
A gradient with respect to the target model
A category-to-score map in which a matching trigger can receive 0.9
A list of prompts selected for PyRIT
questions.explanation: guard_classify initializes every category to 0.0 and raises a category to 0.9 when one of its trigger strings appears. is_unsafe then compares those scores with the threshold, 0.5 by default.

questions.question: How many hazard categories are listed in HAZARD_CATEGORIES?
questions.explanation: The list contains 14 MLCommons-style categories, including privacy, self-harm, indiscriminate weapons, elections, and code-interpreter abuse. The toy only defines triggers for a subset.

questions.question: Which mapping correctly describes Garak's architecture?
options: Probe generates a test, Detector scores the output, and Harness manages the campaign
Probe stores user data, Detector fine-tunes the model, and Harness signs C2PA metadata
Probe is a reward model, Detector is a tokenizer, and Harness is a GPU scheduler
Probe and Detector are both human review queues
questions.explanation: The lesson separates attack generation from scoring and orchestration. GARAK_PROBES supply payloads, garak_scan calls the target and records blocked/detected status, and the surrounding harness runs the set.

questions.question: What does pyrit_campaign add beyond a Garak-style single-turn scan?
options: It removes all converters and sends one seed only
It runs a sequence of seed, paraphrase, encoding, and combined converters until a response is not refused
It requires white-box gradients for every turn
It replaces the target with Llama Guard's category map
questions.explanation: pyrit_campaign logs each converter turn and stops at the first output without the word "refuse". This models an escalating multi-turn campaign rather than independent probes.

questions.question: What production cadence does the lesson recommend for the three tools?
options: Use only manual review after launch
Run PyRIT nightly and never run regression probes
Place Llama Guard around the model, run Garak for recurring regression, and reserve PyRIT for deeper pre-release campaigns
Replace both classifiers with a single static prompt
questions.explanation: The tools cover different surfaces: classifiers gate input/output, Garak provides broad repeatable probes, and PyRIT explores converter chains. Layering and cadence address different failure modes.

questions.question: Why must a red-team report name its judge and refresh its probes?
options: Every judge is guaranteed to agree, so the name is only for formatting
Probe payloads are independent of the target's safety updates
A judge identity determines the model's tokenizer vocabulary
Attack and defense rates depend on the scoring rule and on whether probes remain novel after model patches
questions.explanation: A change in judge criteria can change blocked or successful counts, and a patched model can make an old probe stale. Without both pieces, a regression number is not reproducible or comparable.
